The checker passes 27 of 28 transitions. Transition 27 still fails, and I stopped because the observations cannot explain it.

**What `program.py` does now:**

| Object | Rule |
|---|---|
| Legends in a row | Legends exactly 7 apart are one group. The cursor stops only at the first legend of each group, so x=27 is skipped. |
| Cursor | Its y is the row's y minus 4. Action 4 moves to the next stop, goes to the next row after the last stop, and goes back to row 0 after the last row. Action 3 moves back one stop. |
| Actions 1 and 2 | No visible change in any of the recorded objects. |

**Why transition 27 fails:** One step between transitions 26 and 27 was not recorded, because the cursor moved from x=10 to x=20 between them. In transition 27, action 4 moves the cursor correctly, but `legend_cyan_0` also moves from x=10 to x=11. Nothing in the before state predicts that move. It could be a delayed result of the three action-1 presses at that legend (transitions 24–26), but one example does not confirm this. The recorded objects have no pixel data, so I did not model it. The header comment in `program.py` lists it as an unconfirmed hypothesis.
